2609.08789.title: Silent Revision: Measuring Undisclosed Change in the Safety Frameworks of Frontier AI Developers
2609.08789.paper_summary: Frontier AI developers publish safety frameworks that commit them to evidencing whether their models are dangerous. The European Union and California now treat these documents as instruments of accountability, and both already impose duties on their revision. Neither requires the revision to be legible, in the sense that a reader could learn from the developer's own account what changed. We introduce the silent revision rate, the share of material changes to a framework's commitments that the developer's published account does not identify, and we release the versioned, hash-pinned corpus needed to compute it. The corpus contains every public version of the safety frameworks of the twelve developers that have published one, together with each provider's changelog, redline or announcement. We trace 710 commitment instances across twelve consecutive version pairs, code them against a frozen codebook, and adjudicate 244 individually. Three findings follow. First, 67% of material changes (95% CI 62 to 72) are silent under a strict standard and 53% under a lenient one, falling to 49% at section granularity. Second, silence appears to track the form of the account, since narrative announcements run at 74% against 63% for itemised changelogs, whereas account length in words barely matters; on the test that respects nesting the difference is suggestive. Third, 77% of traced changes weaken or remove a commitment, and in seven of eight pairs weakenings are more often silent than strengthenings. The statutory remedy therefore exists and specifies the wrong artefact. A justification explains why a framework changed, an enumeration states what changed, and only the latter makes revision auditable. We argue that publication duties should carry an enumeration duty, which one provider already meets, voluntarily and incompletely.
2609.08789.paper_summary_zh: 前沿人工智慧開發者發布的安全框架承諾他們將證明其模型是否存在危險。歐盟和加州現在將這些文件視為問責的工具，並且都已經對其修訂施加了義務。兩者都不要求修訂必須清晰易懂，因為讀者無法從開發者自己的說明中了解發生了什麼變化。我們引入了靜默修訂率，即開發者發布的說明中未識別的框架承諾的實質性變更的比例，並釋出計算所需的版本化、哈希固定的語料庫。該語料庫包含了十二位已發布安全框架的開發者的每一個公共版本，以及每個提供者的變更日誌、修訂或公告。我們追踪了十二對連續版本中的710個承諾實例，並根據一個凍結的編碼書對它們進行編碼，並對244個進行個別裁定。以下是三個發現。首先，67%的實質性變更（95% CI 62到72）在嚴格標準下是靜默的，而在寬鬆標準下為53%，在細分到段落層級時降至49%。其次，靜默似乎與說明的形式有關，因為敘述性公告的靜默率為74%，而項目化變更日誌為63%，而說明的字數長度幾乎沒有影響；在尊重嵌套的測試中，差異是暗示性的。第三，77%的追踪變更削弱或移除了承諾，在八對中的七對中，削弱的情況比加強的情況更常靜默。因此，法定救濟措施存在並指定了錯誤的文物。一個理由解釋了為什麼框架發生了變化，列舉說明了什麼變化，只有後者使修訂具有可審計性。我們主張，出版義務應該承擔列舉義務，而其中一位提供者已經自願且不完全地滿足了這一要求。
2609.08789.author: Louis Yiven Zhu et.al.
